edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Hom. in Cant. I, 3

source_text: Osculetur me ergo ab osculis oris sui. Moris est scripturarum imperativum modum pro optativo ponere, ut ibi: Pater noster, qui es in caelis, sanctificetur nomen tuum! pro: utinam sanctificetur; et nunc in praesenti: Osculetur me ab osculis oris sui pro eo, quod est: utinam osculetur. Deinde conspicit sponsum. Venit delibutus unguentis nec aliter ad sponsam poterat venire nec decebat aliter patrem ad nuptias filium destinare. Variis eum unxit unguentis, fecit illum Christum. Venit diversis odoribus spirans et audit: Quia bona ubera tua super vinum. Congrue sermo divinus eandem rem pro locorum qualitate diversis vocabulis nuncupat. Quando hostia offertur in lege et vult intellectus ostendere, pectusculum separationis effatur. Quando vero recumbit aliquis cum Iesu et sensuum eius communione perfruitur, non pectusculum, ut supra, sed pectus eloquitur. Porro cum sponsa loquitur ad sponsum, quia nuptiale carmen inducitur, non pectusculum, ut in sacrificio, non pectus ut in Iohanne discipulo, sed ubera nominat dicens: Quia bona ubera tua super vinum.
pass_a_gloss: May-he-kiss me therefore from kisses of-mouth of-him. Custom is of-scriptures to-put imperative mood for optative, as: Our Father... hallowed-be name yours! for would-that it-be-hallowed; and now: May-he-kiss... for would-that he-kiss. Then she-beholds bridegroom. He-comes anointed with-ointments... varied ointments made him Christ. Divine speech names same-thing with diverse words by place-quality: in law-sacrifice 'little-breast of-separation'; when reclining with Jesus 'breast'; when bride in wedding-song 'breasts' — Because good breasts yours above wine.
notes: Pass A literalist gloss ≠ Pass B literary English.
Song lemma sense-checked against Baehrens; Lawson ACW not used for wording.
pass_b_english: Let him kiss me, then, with the kisses of his mouth. It is the custom of the Scriptures to put the imperative for the optative, as there: [[Our Father who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name >> Bible:Matthew 6:9]]! — for “would that it be hallowed”; and now in the present place: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth, for “would that he kiss me.” Then she catches sight of the Bridegroom. He comes anointed with ointments; he could not come to the Bride otherwise, nor was it fitting that the Father should send the Son to the wedding otherwise. With varied ointments he anointed him and made him Christ. He comes breathing diverse fragrances and hears: [[For your breasts are better than wine >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:2]]. Fittingly the divine word names the same thing with different terms according to the character of the places. When a victim is offered in the law and the sense wants to show it, it says “the little breast of the separation.” But when someone reclines with Jesus and enjoys communion with his thoughts, it does not say “little breast,” as above, but “breast.” And when the Bride speaks to the Bridegroom, because a wedding song is being introduced, she does not name a little breast as in the sacrifice, nor a breast as in the disciple John, but breasts, saying: For your breasts are better than wine.
